Garliava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kauno apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Garliava emerged in the early 19th century, with Jews among its first settlers; the population reached 469 (49 percent) by 1897, and the town was burned down during WWI. In the interwar period, significant emigration to the US, Canada, South Africa, and Palestine took place, while the remaining community maintained a beit-midrash, a Hebrew school, and a Yiddish school. About 70 Jewish families remained in Garliava before WWII; all were murdered by the Germans and their Lithuanian allies.
